previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, a history of kidney transplantation with rejection, and severe aortic stenosis presented with recurrent chest pain and was diagnosed with a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. She was admitted for urgent coronary artery bypass grafting and aortic valve replacement, which were performed on 2157-10-10. The surgery included a triple bypass using the internal mammary artery and saphenous vein grafts, along with replacement of the aortic valve with a 21mm tissue valve. Postoperatively, she recovered well in the CVICU, was extubated early, and transitioned to the telemetry floor. She resumed daily hemodialysis, ambulated with assistance, and showed progressive improvement in lung function and wound healing. She was discharged home on postoperative day 4 in stable condition with instructions for wound care, activity restrictions, and follow-up.

Her pre-operative Isosorbie was resumed at lower dose and can be
